title: Separate a backend readiness failure from an edge policy denial behind client-portal errors
telemetry: Supplied Cloud Logging http_load_balancer request-log entries for a global external Application Load Balancer, with labelled owner observations (a platform-owner backend health view, an edge-security-owner Cloud Armor decision summary and application records), compiled into one export released through a protected fixture CLI. The load balancer and its security policy are global; us-east4 identifies the backend instance group. No live Cloud Logging, Compute Engine or Cloud Armor access.
owner: Ines, Client Portal on-call, owns the investigation; Soren, the edge security owner, owns portal-edge-policy and any Cloud Armor rule decision; Petra, the portal-api application owner, owns release 7.4.0, its readiness behavior and any rollback proposal; Bram, the load-balancing platform owner, owns client-portal-lb, portal-api-mig, the health check and the backend health view. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Ines needs a technical update on the client-portal errors that began around 10:10 UTC. Use the available bounded read interface to inspect the load balancer request records and the labelled owner observations, then report the supported failing step, the evidence and unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner for the existing TLC. No security-policy, health-check, instance-group, release, traffic or firewall change is authorized.
common_evidence:
All projects, load balancer resources, instances, identities and records in this historical packet are synthetic; no real customer request was served.
Window: 2026-10-14T10:00:00Z through 2026-10-14T10:30:00Z; task received at 10:30:00Z.
Scope: project synthetic-clientportal-prod; global external Application Load Balancer client-portal-lb with forwarding rule client-portal-https-fr, target HTTPS proxy client-portal-https-proxy and URL map client-portal-urlmap. The URL map sends /api/* to backend service portal-api-bes and every other path to backend bucket portal-static-bucket.
portal-api-bes serves the regional managed instance group portal-api-mig in us-east4 (6 target instances), uses health check portal-api-hc (HTTP /readyz on port 8080) and has the Cloud Armor backend security policy portal-edge-policy attached.
Interface: the protected fixture CLI accepts bounded read requests and returns supplied sanitized observations; it does not contact Google Cloud.
Change calendar, both entries approved before the window: CHG-7710, portal-api release 7.4.0 rolling update of portal-api-mig, started 10:04:00Z, owner Petra; CHG-7712, portal-edge-policy rule maintenance, applied 10:09:00Z, owner Soren. The calendar summaries do not describe rule content or rollout progress.
Synthetic monitor portal-transfer-quote (POST /api/transfers/quote every 60 s from three locations): baseline 09:00:00Z-10:00:00Z every run passed; from 10:10:00Z through 10:28:00Z every run failed. The monitor reports pass or fail only; it counts any non-2xx response or a 10-second timeout as failed and exports no status code, response body or response header.
Customer support, 10:12:00Z onward: 41 tickets report a generic error page in the client portal, most while submitting a transfer; tickets carry no status code, request ID or timestamp finer than the minute.
Support's own checks at 10:20:00Z: static portal pages load normally.
10:15:00Z operator note: ITO opened the TLC; no rollback, policy edit, health-check change, instance-group change, firewall change or traffic change is approved or recorded beyond the two calendar entries.
The common packet contains no load balancer request-log status breakdown, Cloud Armor decision, backend health state or application record.
Ines is on the existing TLC; Soren, Petra and Bram are reachable through it.

sources.claim: Global external and classic Application Load Balancer logs use resource.type http_load_balancer. statusDetails explains why the load balancer returned its status: failed_to_pick_backend means it failed to pick a healthy backend (502 or 503); denied_by_security_policy means a Cloud Armor policy denied the request, with the status configured in the policy; response_sent_by_backend means the backend's own response was proxied. The fixture's per-request entries and counts are authored.

Cloud Armor request logging records enforcedSecurityPolicy name, outcome (ACCEPT, DENY, REDIRECT and EXEMPT are given as examples), configuredAction, priority and preconfiguredExprIds; previewSecurityPolicy is populated when a preview rule would have taken priority, with its own outcome; a denial has statusDetails denied_by_security_policy. Whether an accepted request that then fails backend selection carries enforcedSecurityPolicy is not documented, so variant A reports Cloud Armor decisions as an owner summary.

Security policies can block traffic before it reaches load-balanced backend services; deny rules can return 403, 404 or 502; a rule can be previewed without enforcement, with its actions noted and both matched and preview rules available in logs. Because a deny can return 502, a status code alone does not separate an edge denial from a backend failure; the case grades statusDetails and policy decisions, not status alone. That a denied request never reached an instance is supplied by the application owner's records, not inferred from the docs.

Unhealthy backends are not eligible to receive new connections; a global external Application Load Balancer returns HTTP 503 when all backends are unhealthy (classic returns 502); probers for GFE-based load balancers use 35.191.0.0/16 and need ingress allow firewall rules. Health check log field names are not given on this page, so the fixture's health view is a labelled owner observation.

Preconfigured WAF rules are named like sqli-v422-stable with signature IDs like owasp-crs-v042200-id942100-sqli; the default sensitivity is 4, and higher sensitivity raises false-positive risk; Google recommends validating rules in preview before they affect production. The fixture reuses the documented example identifiers; which request content matches that signature is not graded.

The http_load_balancer monitored resource (Application Load Balancer) has project_id, forwarding_rule_name, url_map_name, target_proxy_name, backend_service_name and zone labels. Owner health views, policy summaries and application records in this export are labelled supplied records, not native load balancer log fields.

a.conclusion: From 10:09:40 UTC portal-api-bes had no healthy backend. CHG-7710 replaced all six instances with release 7.4.0, whose /readyz returns 503 while the application reports missing ledger.endpoint configuration, so health checks mark every instance unhealthy and the load balancer returns 503 failed_to_pick_backend for every /api/* request. portal-edge-policy enforced no denial; CHG-7712's rule 900 is in preview and its DENY outcomes are logged, not enforced. Probes reach the instances, so a firewall or probe-reachability cause is not supported. Why 7.4.0 lacks the configuration and why the rollout proceeded are not established.
next_checks: Petra confirms why release 7.4.0 starts without ledger.endpoint; Petra and the change approver decide through ITO's change approval between restoring the 7.3.2 instance template and correcting the configuration; this investigation applies neither.
Bram establishes why CHG-7710's rolling update continued while replacement instances failed health checks and reports the healthy backend count on the TLC.

Ines reports recovery only from correlated evidence: HEALTHY backends in Bram's view, /api/* entries with response_sent_by_backend and status 200, and passing monitor runs. Soren reviews the rule 900 preview matches separately before any later enforcement.
unsupported: Attributing the failures to Cloud Armor or the CHG-7712 rule; no enforced DENY is recorded and preview outcomes are not enforced.
Disabling, detaching or editing portal-edge-policy or rule 900 to obtain a passing request.
Loosening portal-api-hc (path, threshold or interval) so instances that report not ready receive traffic, or calling that a fix.
Rolling back, restarting or resizing portal-api-mig as an applied or approved action without the application owner's decision through change approval.
Blaming firewall rules or probe reachability; probes reach the instances and receive 503 from /readyz.
Declaring recovery from one passing request or monitor run.
unknowns: Why the rolling update proceeded while new instances failed health checks.
Whether the 64 preview matches are attacks or legitimate transfers; they do not explain the current failure.
State after the 10:27 owner-record and 10:28 request-log coverage cutoffs.

b.conclusion: Rule priority 900 of portal-edge-policy (preconfigured WAF rule set sqli-v422-stable), switched from preview to enforced by CHG-7712 at 10:09:00 UTC, denies POST /api/transfers requests with 403 denied_by_security_policy, including every synthetic monitor request since 10:10. The backends are healthy: all six instances pass /readyz on 7.4.0, the other /api/* requests return 200 from the backend and no denied transfer request reached an instance. The edge policy, not backend readiness or the rollout, is the failing step for transfers. Which request field matched the signature and whether every denied request is legitimate are not established.
next_checks: Soren reviews the denied entries and the preview-period matches for rule 900, identifies the request field that matched owasp-crs-v042200-id942100-sqli, and decides through change approval between a field exclusion, a sensitivity change, returning the rule to preview or keeping it enforced; this investigation applies none of them.

Petra, with Soren, establishes from sanitized request metadata, starting with the monitor's fixed payload, whether the matched transfer requests are legitimate; customer payloads are not copied into the TLC.

Ines reports recovery only from correlated evidence after an approved policy decision: transfer requests with response_sent_by_backend and status 200, no enforced rule 900 DENY on legitimate traffic, and passing monitor runs.
unsupported: Attributing the failures to the 7.4.0 rollout or backend readiness; backends are HEALTHY and denied requests never reached them.
Restarting, rolling back or scaling portal-api-mig, or loosening portal-api-hc.
Disabling or detaching portal-edge-policy, deleting rule 900 or returning it to preview as an applied fix without the edge security owner's decision through change approval.
Asserting that all denied traffic is benign, or that it is an attack, without reviewing the matched requests.
Treating the 403 as an application authentication or authorization failure.
Declaring recovery from one passing request or monitor run.
unknowns: Which request field matched the signature and whether every denied request is legitimate.
Why the preview-period matches were not reviewed before enforcement.
State after the 10:27 owner-record and 10:28 request-log coverage cutoffs.
